question: Does the E116 cleanup deletion introduce any new swift test failure?
answer: No. The unmodified assignment base produces the identical failure profile: the same 9 tests, the same 40 issues, and the same per-test issue counts.

base.tree: detached worktree at the assignment base
base.abort_reason: MLX error: Failed to load the default metallib. library not found (Vendor/mlx-swift/.../random.cpp:143). A fresh worktree has no built mlx.metallib. The abort happens after every one of the 40 issues is already recorded.
base.note: The abort is a worktree artefact, not a source difference. tools/build-mlx-metallib.sh writes mlx.metallib into the main checkout only.

the_one_test_that_touches_a_file_i_edite.my_only_edit: deleted the 4-line E58DispatchCensus.installIfRequested() hook and its comment
the_one_test_that_touches_a_file_i_edite.conclusion: The observed values equal the base source literals exactly. A stale test expectation that was not updated when the 512 MiB referenced-byte budget was promoted. No environment variable is involved; the run environment holds no MLX_* variables.

unchanged_inputs_vs_base: No docs, fixtures, manifests, workflow files, benchmark.json, setup or benchmark scripts changed. Every failing test other than startupMemoryPolicyKeepsRanked128GiBProfile reads only those unchanged inputs.
